theory.intro: The **highest common factor (HCF)** of two numbers is the largest whole number that divides into both of them exactly.
facts: A **common factor** divides both numbers with no remainder.
$1$ is a common factor of every pair, so the HCF is at least $1$.
Factors of $12$ are $1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12$ and factors of $18$ are $1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18$, so the HCF is $6$.
steps: List the factors of each number.
Identify the factors common to both.
The HCF is the largest of the common factors.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the highest common factor of $30$ and $42$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Factors of $30$: $1$, $2$, $3$, $5$, $6$, $10$, $15$, $30$.
Factors of $42$: $1$, $2$, $3$, $6$, $7$, $14$, $21$, $42$.
The common factors are $1$, $2$, $3$ and $6$.
The largest common factor is $6$.
$\text{HCF}=6$

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the HCF in each case.
(a) $22$ and $66$
(b) $14$ and $25$
Explain why the HCF in (a) is one of the given numbers, while the HCF in (b) is $1$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Factors of $22$: $1$, $2$, $11$, $22$.
Factors of $66$: $1$, $2$, $3$, $6$, $11$, $22$, $33$, $66$.
The common factors are $1$, $2$, $11$ and $22$.
$\text{HCF}=22$
The smaller number $22$ divides $66$ exactly, so all factors of $22$ are shared. No factor of $22$ can be greater than $22$.
(b) Factors of $14$: $1$, $2$, $7$, $14$.
Factors of $25$: $1$, $5$, $25$.
Only $1$ is in both lists.
$\text{HCF}=1$
There is no shared factor greater than $1$.
